From: Sara Tanner <sara.tanner@orbithealth.com>

Cc: support@orbithealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 Dec 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partial service degrade during cache failover — request for credit eligibility

Hi Soojin,

We observed a customer-facing increase in 5xx and tail latency for approximately 12 minutes this morning (see timestamps below). Many requests hit stale cache paths while a failover to the secondary cache cluster occurred. Our telemetry shows a sharp TPS drop and then a gradual recovery.

Details:
- Window: 2027-12-20T09:03:20Z — 2027-12-20T09:15:45Z (UTC)
- Affected endpoints: /v1/generate, /v1/chat/stream
- Impact: ~8% error rate spike, 300–800ms additional p95 for ~12 minutes

We'd like to confirm whether this incident qualifies for an SLA credit (partial degradation) and whether the maintenance window exclusion applies. We saw a maintenance flag in the control plane around 09:00 UTC but no customer notification was listed in our console. Attached are sample request logs and a CSV of cache snapshots.

Attachments: cache-snapshots-20271220.csv, orbithealth-request-logs.zip

Can you advise eligibility and next steps?

Thanks,
Sara Tanner
Infrastructure Lead, OrbitHealth

Quick next steps from my side:

- Jonas, can SRE validate whether the event meets our "partial degradation" criteria and whether a third-party CDN or peering issue contributed?

I'll loop back with a preliminary answer within a business day. If this meets SLA credit criteria, we'll prepare a credit calculation and the supporting telemetry.

Best,

I pulled the customer notification and maintenance history: there was an internal control-plane rollout scheduled starting 2027-12-20T08:55:00Z to 2027-12-20T09:05:00Z labeled "cache routing improvements". That rollout was marked by the engineering team as low-risk and not customer-impacting in the change ticket, but it looks like the flag was set in a way that did not surface in the customer console — that's a gap.

Given the lack of visible customer notification, we should treat this as a customer-impact incident for the purposes of SLA review and not assume automatic maintenance exclusion.

Subject: Re: Partial service degrade during cache failover — request for credit eligibility

Short SRE summary and timeline below (attaching a sanitized extract of our probe and edge metrics).

Observed timeline (UTC):
- 2027-12-20T09:02:10Z — control plane route update propagated to 2/3 edge nodes
- 2027-12-20T09:03:25Z — increased 5xx observed on upstreams; failed cache read rate increases
- 2027-12-20T09:06:40Z — automated cache failover completed; KV sync in progress
- 2027-12-20T09:15:45Z — latency and error rates returned to baseline

Root cause notes:
- The route update triggered a short window where a subset of edge nodes referenced stale cache shards while KV sync completed; that produced transient elevated p95 and a small 5xx spike.
- No third-party CDN outage was observed in our vendor telemetry; however, we did see higher error rates on egress to one peering fabric at 09:03–09:05 which correlated with increased end-to-end latency for affected customers. That peering blip amplified the user surface impact by ~20% vs. what a pure internal failover would have produced.

SLA decision guidance (based on our policy):
- "Maintenance exclusion" applies when a maintenance window is both scheduled and visible to the customer dashboard AND the change is recorded with a customer-impact flag. In this case the change was scheduled internally but did not surface to the customer, so exclusion should not be automatically applied.
- "Partial degradation" threshold: external error rate >5% or sustained p95 delta >250ms for >5 minutes. For this event, p95 delta peaked ~450ms and the error spike lasted ~12 minutes, so it meets partial degradation criteria.

Recommendation: approve a pro-rata SLA credit covering the 12-minute window. I recommend we base the credit on the customer's committed SLA (99.95%) and use our standard apportionment for combined internal + peering amplification. I'll attach the metric extract and sample probes.

Attachments referenced: cache-snapshots-20271220.csv (from customer), redwood-probes-20271220-extract.csv [attached], apportionment-calculation.pdf [internal].

Jonas Weber
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
